output.brief:
The soft-pedal complaints are mainly a brake-fluid problem in vans serviced at Northfield Motor Services during the bay closure, not a driver or Upper Wend problem. All 11 complaint vans were among the 13 Northfield vans. Northfield topped up fluid from a bulk drum that had taken on water. The two warranty returns measured 152°C and 149°C boiling point against 255°C for sealed stock, and the technician linked this to soft pedals on long descents. Drivers logged no brake reports in other vans, including 141 Upper Wend days, and Calder Road and in-house vans on the same Tessaro pads had no complaints. So the Tessaro pads, driver technique, and FleetCheck reporting do not explain the cluster. I'm fairly confident, though the fluid link rests on two measured vans and no one has tested the rest.

Next steps this week: take the Northfield-serviced vans out of service until their fluid is tested and renewed from sealed stock. Start with LK-214 and LK-227 as well, since they were done later. Don't issue warnings or require retraining; that would punish drivers for reporting a real fault and discourage future reports. Hold off on switching pad suppliers. Also follow up Okafor's 25 September recheck request, which has no reply on file.
